title: NetBird VPS vs Proxmox, Coolify API/MCP, backup teaser, Cloudflare Tunnel
summary: Four Ed-selected topics: prefer a public VPS for NetBird self-host now (Proxmox later with stable IP + UDP 3478); drive Coolify via scoped API tokens, IP allowlist, and official MCP/CLI (read-first); a short public teaser on why ransomware empties “good” backups (full pack stays on Secure); reduce Coolify dashboard exposure with Cloudflare Tunnel while keeping 80/443 for apps. Overheard: Astra rollout guide + Siri↔Claude/ChatGPT swap coverage.

sections.heading: NetBird self-host designs: VPS vs Proxmox
bullets: Two SMB-sized designs with Authentik + Coolify: (A) NetBird control plane on a public VPS; (B) NetBird on a Proxmox VM behind edge NAT — Coolify hosts join as netbird-client in both.

Shared requirements (official self-host path): public reachability on TCP 80/443 and UDP 3478 (embedded STUN cannot ride an HTTP reverse proxy); public DNS; Traefik (or equivalent) for HTTP/2 + gRPC; Authentik as Generic OIDC IdP.

Design A — VPS Pros: matches NetBird quickstart; clean public ports; isolates mesh control plane from Coolify/SMB blast radius. Cons: VPS cost; relay bandwidth; single-region SPOF until external relays.

Design B — Proxmox Pros: on-prem control plane; snapshots/PBS; no VPS bill. Cons: needs stable public IP (or 1:1 NAT) with inbound UDP 3478; CGNAT/residential is painful; mesh uptime couples to site power/ISP; prefer a VM over LXC for the server stack.
Coolify ships netbird-client one-click, not NetBird server — join hosts with a setup key and NB_MANAGEMENT_URL at your self-hosted management.

Recommendation: Design A (public VPS) for Ed now — least friction for 80/443 + UDP 3478 and keeps the control plane off Coolify’s app host. Revisit Proxmox only with confirmed inbound UDP 3478 and a real sovereignty need.

sections.heading: Coolify API + MCP for Grok Bot automation
bullets: Coolify REST API (`/api/v1/…`) uses Bearer tokens scoped to one team (`read`, `read:sensitive`, `write`, `deploy`, `root`). Enable API Access and Allowed IPs so only trusted egress reaches the API.
Official Coolify MCP: Streamable HTTP at `https://<instance>/mcp` with the same team token; start with `read` — sensitive values are redacted; revoke the token to cut MCP off.
Official coolify-cli covers scripted/CI over the same API. Community stdio MCP bridges exist; prefer first-party `/mcp` when the agent can reach the instance over HTTPS.

Pros: inventory, deploys, and troubleshooting without click-ops; scopes + IP allowlist limit blast radius. Cons: `root` / `write`+`read:sensitive` tokens are high-value if leaked; bad allowlists lock agents out or leave the API wide open.

Recommendation: restrictive IP allowlist; dedicated team token with `read` first (add `deploy` only when intentional); official MCP before community bridges; never put `root` or long-lived `read:sensitive` on an always-on agent.

sections.heading: Backup & ransomware — public teaser only
bullets: Problem frame: many teams discover too late that “we have backups” still fails under ransomware — copies that live online with production get encrypted or deleted, and untested restores are not recoverability.
Public takeaway (CISA-aligned): keep at least one copy attackers cannot reach from the production admin plane, and actually test a restore — a green backup job is not proof you can come back.
Coolify-specific public tip: instance DB dumps without a separately saved `APP_KEY` (off-box) restore into an unreadable secrets vault — see Coolify’s own backup docs.

Paywall boundary: Digest stays teaser-only on this topic. The full Backup & Crypto Resilience reference plan (frameworks, maturity questions, playbooks, vignettes) ships on the members library at secure.efortune.tech — not here.

sections.heading: Coolify Cloudflare Tunnel for dashboard exposure
bullets: Official path: run `cloudflared` (Coolify one-click), point tunnel routes at `http://localhost:80` (Coolify proxy), publish apps via domains — Cloudflare terminates visitor HTTPS.
Dashboard exposure: default installs often leave UI/realtime on ~8000 / 6001 / 6002 reachable on the public IP even when apps use a custom domain.
Hardening: bind Coolify UI to localhost only (or override ports empty on `coolify` / `soketi`) so the dashboard is not on the public NIC — reach admin through tunnel/VPN while apps keep 80/443.
Pros: hides origin IP, helps CGNAT/home gear. Cons: depends on Cloudflare; tunnels bypass host firewall for tunneled paths; NetBird/STUN UDP still cannot ride an HTTP tunnel.
Recommendation: Tunnel (or CF proxy) for apps on 80/443; close or localhost-bind 8000/6001/6002; prefer VPN/ZTNA or strict allowlist for the Coolify dashboard — not public IP:8000.

bottomLine: Host NetBird’s control plane on a public VPS for now (Proxmox later only with stable IP + inbound UDP 3478). Automate Coolify with scoped read-first API/MCP tokens plus an IP allowlist — not root tokens. Ransomware backups: Digest only teases the failure mode; the deep reference plan stays on secure.efortune.tech. Expose apps via Cloudflare Tunnel on 80/443; close Coolify’s 8000/6001/6002 and gate the dashboard with VPN/allowlist.
